subject: Finlytics latency spike after v9.2 rollout — rollback or temporary SLA carveout?

Cc: ops+SRE@finlytics.com, Finlytics Procurement <procure@finlytics.com>
Date: 2029-04-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Increased p95 after v9.2 rollout — urgent assistance requested

Hi Jordan,

We pushed model v9.2 to production for the default text-generation route at 05:30 PT this morning and have been seeing sustained p95 latency climb from ~420ms to ~1.9s for user-facing requests over the last three hours. The spike correlates with the rollout window; attached is a short CSV with minute-level p95/success-rate and a trace extract.

This is impacting real-time features for two of our key flows (payment auth and fraud scoring). Our SRE team is seeing increased queuing on the GPU side and a KV caching miss pattern that wasn't present on v9.1.

We need to understand options ASAP: can Redwood perform an emergency rollback to v9.1, or do we need an SLA carveout while you investigate? If rollback is possible, we also need the attendant authorization/contract note for procurement in order to avoid downstream billing disputes.

Attached: latency-snapshot-20290420.csv, upload-trace-20290420.txt

Thanks — Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Engineering, Finlytics

Jordan / team — quick triage notes from SRE:

- Correlation: spike aligns precisely with control-plane rollout of v9.2 at 05:30 PT; rolling window shows baseline p95 returning for a small fraction of traffic that hits warmed KV caches. Global failure mode is increased sample-level attention cache misses when sequence prefix variability is high (Finlytics uses long context in fraud scoring).
- Execution path: v9.2 introduced a quantized attention kernel that reduces memory but at the cost of fallback code-paths for certain token patterns (we see more fallbacks at 97th+ percentile). Those fallbacks trigger synchronous memory compaction that increases latency under concurrency.
- Repro: internal canary on identical workload reproduced the p95 increase within 30 minutes; v9.1 baseline is stable.

Suggested mitigations (ranked):
A) Emergency rollback to v9.1 on Finlytics tenant — low-risk, immediate p95 reduction. Requires ops sign-off + customer acceptance for traffic interruption and a short verification window (10–15 minutes).
B) Pin traffic to v9.1 via routing (70% v9.1 / 30% v9.2) and enable aggressive KV warm-up for 24–48h — reduced impact but slower full mitigation.
C) Apply a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap to reduce compaction triggers while we patch v9.2 quant kernel (estimated fix ETA 48–72h).

I recommend path A for Finlytics given production impact on payment auth. For the emergency rollback we need the following: ops approval (Markus), explicit customer authorization (Elena), and a short procurement amendment to document a rollback-triggered billing adjustment. I've attached a short trace extract and a dashboard link.

Attachments referenced: finlytics-slo-dashboard-link.txt (dashboard snapshot), upload-trace-20290420.txt

-naomi
